title: WAN
notes: None — an extender has no internet connection of its own. It reaches the internet through the gateway, over its mesh backhaul link.

title: LAN
notes: An Ethernet port lets the extender use a wired backhaul link to the gateway instead of Wi-Fi, when one is available.

title: Wi-Fi

detail.label: Mesh
detail.value: Acts as an EasyMesh agent, joining a gateway's mesh to extend its coverage

notes: Wi-Fi access point for wireless devices, covering 2.4, 5, and 6 GHz bands. Also used for the wireless mesh backhaul link back to the gateway.

title: Bluetooth / IoT

detail.label: Tested with
detail.value: TP-Link Tapo smart plug (Matter over Wi-Fi), onvis smart plug (Matter over Thread)

notes: Same multiprotocol radio as the gateway, for connecting smart-home devices if IoT support is enabled on the extender.

title: Packet Processor
notes: Present on the board, but unused — an extender doesn't route or NAT traffic, so there's nothing for this to accelerate.

title: AI / NPU
notes: Not present on this hardware today. A future board revision could add one as a plug-in module, for on-device AI features.

title: USB
notes: A general-purpose USB port, available for connecting IoT devices during testing.

title: SIM Card Slot
notes: Present on the board, but unused — this profile has no cellular backup feature.

title: Storage
notes: Onboard flash storage for the firmware, with A/B partitions so updates can be applied safely.

title: SD Card Slot
notes: A removable SD card slot, present on this hardware.

title: Media Tuner
notes: No tuner hardware — an extender has no WAN or voice functions.

title: Debug Port
notes: A serial console and JTAG access for low-level debugging during development.

title: WPS Button
notes: A physical button for quick Wi-Fi setup, so a new device can join without typing a password.

title: Reset Button
notes: A physical button to restore the extender to its factory default settings.

title: Power Button
notes: A physical power switch for the device.
